title: Radhe Shyam Bansal v. State of U.P.
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Sunita Agarwal and Krishan Pahal, JJ.
disposition: Writ petition dismissed; mandamus for new connection refused.
headnote: The Allahabad High Court dismissed a writ seeking mandamus for a new electricity connection where a prior connection in the same premises had been disconnected with outstanding dues of Rs. 49,359. Applying Clause 4.3 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, the Division Bench held that a new connection cannot be provided while such dues remain unpaid, and that the petitioner's unexplained claim of residence did not make the case fit for mandamus.
facts: Radhe Shyam Bansal sought a writ mandamus for a new electricity connection to a house. After a short adjournment for instructions, the licensee stated that a prior connection in the name of Dharmendra Raghav, son of Jaspal Raghav, had been disconnected on 26 August 2021 with outstanding dues of Rs. 49,359, and that a fresh connection could not be given until those dues were cleared. The petitioner claimed to be a permanent resident of the house but did not state how or when he came into possession.

holding_units.topic: new connection barred by outstanding premises dues
holding_units.holding: Clause 4.3 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 provides that a new connection cannot be given where electricity dues remain outstanding on the premises. Mandamus will not issue to compel a fresh connection in that situation; an unexplained claim of residence does not make the case fit for a writ.

principle_tags.application: The Court treated outstanding dues of Rs. 49,359 on a prior disconnected connection as a Clause 4.3 bar to mandamus for a new connection in the same premises, and dismissed the writ.
